text:
rachel.sales: quick help requested  POC for NorthArc (tenant northarc-poc) is stalled. They connected Azure AD enterprise app for SAML + SCIM. Azure says provisioning succeeded (shows 204/200 in UI) but our tenant still has 0 users. SAML assertion seems to use NameID=transient. also customer asks if they can get a temporary hosted key to run a Dedicated pool throughput smoke test while we debug provisioning. cc @min.eng @eli.se
min.eng: azure is a little different from Okta. 204 in their UI can be misleading  it means Azure received a 2xx from our endpoint. If we returned 409/403/401 at a later step Azure may still mark it as success. Do you have the provisioning logs or a raw request example?
rachel.sales: i asked them for the provisioning audit log. they pasted the SAML sample they see in the SSO test tool: 
```xml
<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion">
  <saml:Subject>
    <saml:NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient">_t_9a2b\</saml:NameID>
  </saml:Subject>
  <saml:AttributeStatement>
    <saml:Attribute Name="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress">
      <saml:AttributeValue>alice@northarc.com</saml:AttributeValue>
    </saml:Attribute>
  </saml:AttributeStatement>
</saml:Assertion>
```
eli.se: transient NameID is fine if the assertion includes an email claim AS WELL (which it does here). Our SSO mapping will accept either NameID=emailAddress or the email claim. The bigger red flag is SCIM. What does Azure map for 'userName' / 'externalId'?
rachel.sales: their provisioning mapping screenshot shows: userName -> user.userPrincipalName, externalId -> group.id (they were doing group-based provisioning).
min.eng: externalId mapped to group.id can cause duplicates in group pushes (we've seen Azure flatten group members into multiple pushes). Our SCIM API treats externalId as a unique key and will reject duplicates with 409. Azure may still mark the provisioning attempt as success. We should look at our SCIM logs for tenant northarc-poc.
security-bot: note: for Private/VPC trials we require SCIM traffic only from allowed IP ranges or via mTLS depending on contract. If NorthArc sits behind a corporate proxy that terminates TLS and rewrites Authorization headers we will see 401/403. Also never paste tokens in screenshots.
viv.ops: checking logs now  we see repeated 409s for externalId=group_88 followed by a single 403 where Authorization header was missing. That matches two problems: duplicate externalId and a proxy stripping the header intermittently. Also, Azure sometimes uses a different bearer token field for SCIM; they must configure the Bearer token in the provisioning connector settings, not the SSO SAML setup.
eli.se: actionable fixes: 1) ask them to change SCIM user mapping: set userName and externalId to user.userPrincipalName or user.mail (we prefer user.userPrincipalName for Azure). 2) ensure the SCIM bearer token in Azure's provisioning app is set to the SCIM service token we provide (scim_service_***). 3) keep NameID as email OR map the email claim explicitly. Sample Azure mapping we can share:
```json
{
  "userName": "user.userPrincipalName",
  "externalId": "user.userPrincipalName",
  "emails": ["user.mail"]
}
```
rachel.sales: they'll ask if we can create a temporary hosted key to run a 1-hour Dedicated throughput validation on pool `dedicated-northarc-1` while they fix provisioning. They said they need to run a short load test for their SLA docs.
viv.ops: we can issue a scoped short-lived key. But important: hosted API keys do NOT authenticate SCIM calls. SCIM requires the SCIM service token. If they copied the hosted onboarding API key into Azure's provisioning connector that's likely the 403. I'll create two creds: scim_service_northarc_24h (scoped to /scim endpoints) and tmp_infer_northarc_1h (scoped to inference:generate and restricted to pool dedicated-northarc-1). We'll DM the secrets only to the named POC admin.
security-bot: reminder: for hosted trials bearer tokens are acceptable but we restrict model list and pool access. For Private/Prem deployments we may require mTLS or IP allowlist; confirm contract. Also advise the customer not to upload tokens to the ticketing system.
aad-bot: SCIM provisioning from aad.northarc.com -> /scim/v2/Users returned 409 at 1908765502 (duplicate externalId=group_88)
min.eng: once they change externalId->user.userPrincipalName and swap the Bearer token to the new scim_service token, they should trigger a manual provisioning cycle and watch for 201/200 events. If they still see 204 in Azure but no users, ask them to capture the raw HTTP request/response pair (headers+body) from their side. Example curl to check auth from their network:
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer SCIM_SERVICE_TOKEN_GOES_HERE" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  https://scim.redwood-inference.example.com/scim/v2/ServiceProviderConfig
```
rachel.sales: thanks  i've requested their Azure admin swap mappings and confirm the Bearer token field is updated. viv, can you create the two tokens and DM me the secrets? i'll only pass them to the designated admin over DM.
viv.ops: created tokens: scim_service_northarc_24h (expires=1908851832), tmp_infer_northarc_1h (key_id=tmp_nr_1h, expires=1908769032, scopes=[inference:generate], pool=[dedicated-northarc-1], allowed_models=[benchmark-lite]). secrets DM'ed to Rachel. Annotation: rotate on expiry.
rachel.sales: received and DM'ed to NorthArc admin with the Azure mapping example and SAML snippet. requested manual repro and raw logs if they still see issues. will update thread when provisioning completes. thanks all.
eli.se: if they want, i can paste a minimal SAML metadata file and step-by-step Azure Enterprise App screenshots.
rachel.sales: pls do that if they ask. closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
